newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil up on China purchase talk - trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil up on China purchase talk - trade.

text.p: Rumors that China bought at least 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil sent CBOT soyoil futures higher on Friday, U.S. exporters and traders said.
"Supposedly, China bought 15,000 tonnes of soyoil," a soyoil exporter said. It could well be that China had a purchase on already from a major U.S. exporter and they are just covering it, he said.
It may not be new business, the trader noted.
"There is business going on," another soyoil exporter said. The 15,000 tonnes sold to China is a "good possbility," he said.
Soyoil was also bolstered by the fact that South American soyoil prices did not go down very much, he said.
Cargill Inc was a noted buyer of CBOT soyoil futures, traders said.
At 1045 CST, December soybean oil was up 0.15 cent to 22.70 cents per lb after touched a session high of 22.83 cents.
Soymeal was lower on commercial spreading of soyoil/soymeal, sources said.
December soymeal was $2.40 a ton lower to $1.50 higher with December down $2.40 at $217.10 per ton. Contract lows were set in January through August as well as the October 1997 contract.
